questions.q: What is the primary dramatic function of the character 'Director' (फुंस'क) in the play "जतूह"? State in one sentence.
questions.a: The Director represents institutional authority that perpetuates a contradictory system: he acknowledges the futility of tuition ("बच्चे देक्क्सज नहीं, गक्सफ'क;ज है") yet refuses to reform the system, exposing bureaucratic complicity. A wrong answer (e.g., "He is the villain who hates students") reveals the student confuses character role with moral judgment, missing the systemic critique.

questions.q: Explain why Jatuh's statement "अच्छा है तो फिर दो, हमारे साथ---मरो, इस बेजा को" (Act 3) is an instance of dramatic irony. What does the audience know that the Principal does not?
questions.a: The irony lies in Jatuh inviting the Principal to join her protest against the tuition system, while the audience knows the Principal is powerless to change it because he is bound by the same bureaucratic rules (he later admits "नियम...बेजा नहीं बदल सकते"). A wrong answer focusing only on Jatuh's anger misses the structural irony: the system traps both teacher and administrator.

questions.q: Apply the concept of 'foil' to analyze how Yashoda (यशोदा) and Jatuh (जतूह) function as contrasting responses to the same oppressive system. Provide one textual evidence for each.
questions.a: Yashoda internalizes oppression ("हम लोग तो नौकरी करते हैं...चुपचाप सहते हैं"), while Jatuh resists ("मैं कहती हूँ...नहीं मानूँगी"). Evidence: Yashoda says "अच्छा जी...मैं समझ गई" (submission); Jatuh says "नहीं, मैं नहीं मानूँगी" (defiance). A wrong answer listing traits without contrasting their *agency* shows misunderstanding of foil as a structural device.

questions.q: Analyze the significance of the stage direction "नक़ल...नक़ल...नक़ल" (repeated thrice) in the tuition scene. How does this repetition function at literal, symbolic, and thematic levels simultaneously?
questions.a: Literally: students mindlessly copy. Symbolically: education reduced to mechanical reproduction. Thematically: critiques a system valuing rote output over understanding. The triple repetition mirrors the three tuition subjects (Physics, Chemistry, Maths) and the three-way complicity (parents, tutors, schools). A wrong answer treating it as mere emphasis misses the layered signification.

questions.q: Evaluate the playwright's choice to end the play with Jatuh and her sister eating "पूरी-सब्जी" while discussing the new tuition ban rule. Does this ending undermine or strengthen the play's critique? Justify.
questions.a: It strengthens the critique through bitter realism: the mundane meal contrasts with the revolutionary meeting, showing that systemic change doesn't alter daily survival. The sister's pragmatic "नौकरी तो करनी है" (must keep the job) undercuts Jatuh's idealism, leaving the audience with unresolved tension — the hallmark of social realism. A wrong answer calling it a "happy ending" ignores the subtext of compromise.

questions.q: Create a 4-line monologue for Vimal (विमल) ten years later, reflecting on his 72 marks in Home Science. It must reveal his current perspective on the tuition culture he experienced.
questions.a: A strong monologue: "बहत्तर नंबर लाया था घरेलू विज्ञान में, / ट्यूशन के बावजूद, ट्यूशन के कारण नहीं। / आज जब मेरा बेटा रोता है फीस के लिए, / मैं कहता हूँ: बेटा, नंबर नहीं, हुनर कमा।" A weak answer (e.g., "I got good marks, tuition helped") fails to show character growth or thematic resonance, indicating the student cannot project textual evidence into imaginative extension.
